title: Add mixed-workload scenarios + SLO-tier pass/fail thresholds (fast/standard/cost-efficient)
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Context: Runtime is shipping workload-aware batching defaults with three customer-facing latency SLO tiers (fast / standard / cost-efficient). The benchmark-lab perf suite needs tier-aligned mixed-workload scenarios + deterministic pass/fail gates so perf-canary can block regressions by tier.

This PR adds: (1) mixed-workload scenarios that combine short/medium/long prompts + streaming/non-streaming in the same run, with concurrency ramps; (2) tier-specific latency targets and gating logic aligned to the formal SLO tier doc; (3) reporting updates so CI artifacts clearly show which tier failed, at which percentile, and which scenario component (streaming vs non-streaming, long-tail vs bulk).

What changed (high level): - New scenario definitions under scenarios/slo_tiers/ covering: chat_streaming_mixed, summarize_nonstream_mixed, and codegen_mixed (blend of completion-style and chat-format). Each scenario includes a fixed prompt-length distribution (buckets) and a concurrency ramp (low → mid → peak) to expose queueing pathologies. - Introduced a tier threshold registry (fast/standard/cost_efficient) that maps scenario → metric → allowed percentile budget. Currently we gate on: TTFT p95/p99 (streaming only), end-to-end latency p95/p99 (non-streaming only), and steady-state tokens/sec drop vs baseline. - Updated gate runner to emit structured failure reasons used downstream by perf-canary (tier, metric, percentile, observed, threshold, and notes).

Alignment: Threshold numbers are pulled from the latency SLO tiers definition doc, with two benchmark-lab specific adaptations: (a) we gate on scenario-specific subsets (e.g., TTFT only for streaming scenarios) and (b) we include a small noise margin for GPU scheduling jitter, bounded and documented.

Notes/constraints: - These scenarios are designed to be workload-representative, not exhaustive. They intentionally stress mixed lengths to catch starvation/regression in continuous batching heuristics. - Default thresholds are intended for hosted baseline hardware profiles; Dedicated/Private clusters can still run the suite but should treat results as informational unless they pin identical hardware + driver stack.

Rollout: - Land scenarios + gates behind BENCHMARK_SLO_TIER_GATES=1 (default on in CI, but can be disabled locally). - Perf-canary will start consuming tier labels from the JSON artifact in a follow-up.

Checklist: - [x] Added new scenarios + docs - [x] Added tier threshold registry - [x] Updated gate runner output schema + examples - [x] Validated on A100 + H100 runners (2 seeds each) - [x] Added baseline regeneration notes for INT-33055 process
commits: benchmark: add mixed prompt-length distributions + concurrency ramps
gates: introduce tier threshold registry + reason-coded failures
reporting: emit per-tier JSON artifact for perf-canary consumption
docs: describe new scenario families + how to tune noise margin
